positive_feedback: Genuine 1:1 structural mirror of shared[T,N]: crates/axc-hir/src/local.rs is a near-verbatim copy-rename of shared.rs (same doc structure, same const-naming pattern MAX_LOCAL_ARRAY_ELEMS/MAX_LOCAL_ARRAY_BYTES/LOCAL_ARRAY_SPILL_ADVISORY_BYTES mirroring MAX_SHARED_ELEMS/MAX_SHARED_BYTES, same elem_byte_size/total_byte_size/needs_* methods, same is_allowed_local_element signature and doc style, same test naming convention). crates/axc-codegen/src/local.rs mirrors shared.rs equally closely, with the Function-vs-Workgroup OpVariable-placement divergence documented prominently and correctly at the top of the module doc comment.

codegen prelude/emit wiring (body.rs, emit.rs) exactly matches spec section 7/9/12.2: OpVariable created only in the entry-block prelude loop after the let-scalar loop, LocalArrayDeclMarker is a no-op dispatch mirroring SharedDeclMarker, and all four recursion helpers (expr_uses_gid, expr_uses_local_invocation_id, expr_uses_subgroup_op, expr_uses_coopmat) plus their stmt-level counterparts got LocalArrayRead/LocalArrayWrite/LocalArrayDeclMarker arms, symmetric with the existing Shared* arms.

Bidirectional name-collision guard (spec section 8, r2's #1 mandated fix) is implemented in both directions exactly as specified: register_local_array checks shared_name_map (typecheck.rs ~line 995-240) and register_shared was extended to check local_array_name_map (typecheck.rs ~line 972-189) -- this is the correctness-critical fix and it is genuinely present in the code, not just asserted in the spec prose. QA independently reproduced both orders with fresh fixtures.

Nested-decl rejection (section 5.1) is implemented with a nice touch beyond the literal spec text: check_local_array_decl_stmt still calls register_local_array before rejecting (poisoning the name) so later in-block uses resolve as local-array references instead of cascading into UnknownBinding/IndexOnNonBuffer noise -- documented clearly in the function doc comment, and QA independently verified zero-cascade behavior.

Const-OOB check (section 5.2) is a clean, minimal, symmetric addition (local_array_const_index_oob helper used identically in both check_local_array_read and check_local_array_write) with an exact boundary (v >= len) and an explicit unit test (at_2944_const_index_oob_boundary_exact) covering in-bounds, at-N, and symbolic cases.

examples/local_histogram.axc is idiomatic and matches the existing corpus's style (for i in range(...) matches reduction.axc; gid(0u32) matches other examples; anti-pattern #2 explicit return; documented). It genuinely exercises every new surface named in section 10 (decl, zero-init loop, indexed RMW, indexed read, u32 index typing, aggregate cap far under threshold) in a small, obviously-correct kernel.

DESIGN.md S3.1.44 is accurate and complete: correctly states Function-vs-Workgroup divergence, the 4096/1024 byte thresholds (16x tighter than shared's 65536, matches local.rs consts), the two hazard classes with the honest path-insensitivity disclosure carried over verbatim from the spec, the nested-scope restriction rationale, the bidirectional collision-guard description, an accurate Files list, and an accurate AT range summary. The S3.1 type table and S3.2 annotation table also got matching one-line additions.

The AT-2918 re-pin is clean: assertion logic (every added line must be exactly 'opt_log: None,', zero removed lines) is byte-for-byte preserved; only the comparison range changed from a live working-tree-vs-HEAD diff to fixed SHAs (cb750ec..6c7732d) with a graceful skip-on-unavailable fallback mirroring AT-2607's existing pattern. This correctly fixes the problem the prior doc comment itself flagged (a live-HEAD gate would false-fail on every future codegen-touching milestone) rather than silently deleting the test.

LOC self-report is honest: QA independently reconciled the coder's per-file breakdown against raw git --numstat and found near-exact-to-exact matches; the +715 (35.75%) overage vs the 2000 cap is disclosed, not hidden, and is pre-authorized by the milestone spec's own section 12 concession that overage toward 2000 is expected.

Capability-flag match arms (emit_local_array_types) are verbatim copies of emit_shared_globals's match block including the explicit comment about observe_type not covering F16 -- correct per spec section 7, and emit.rs correctly ORs local_array_pre_caps into the merged capability set alongside shared_pre_caps.

minor_issues.description: The reused error variant for the register_shared-side collision is TypecheckError::SharedNameCollision rather than a name that says 'collides with a local array' -- functionally correct and QA-verified to fire, but a reader diffing error variant names against the LocalArrayNameCollision used on the register_local_array side might momentarily wonder why the two directions report different variant names for the same class of collision. Cosmetic; not spec-violating (the spec only requires the collision be caught bidirectionally, not that the variant names match).

HirError::LocalArrayTooLarge in validate.rs is dead code (validate() has no caller outside its own tests), same as the pre-existing SharedMemoryTooLarge gap it mirrors. This is explicitly disclosed in the code's own doc comment and in QA's report as a pre-existing, unrelated issue M3.20 does not worsen -- flagging only so it doesn't get missed in a future dead-code sweep.

summary: APPROVE. This is a textbook mirror milestone: crates/axc-hir/src/local.rs and crates/axc-codegen/src/local.rs are genuine copy-rename derivatives of shared.rs (verified side-by-side), the two deliberate divergences (Function-storage entry-block-prelude OpVariable placement, no runtime metadata) are correctly implemented and clearly documented at every layer, and the three r2 surgical fixes (bidirectional collision guard, nested-decl rejection, const-OOB hard error) are all genuinely present in code -- not just asserted in the spec -- and independently verified by QA with fresh, non-reused fixtures against the real lex->parse->HIR pipeline. Parser recovery reports ALL errors in one pass (AT-2929 verified with 3 distinct malformed decls -> 3 distinct error variants). DESIGN.md S3.1.44 is accurate. The AT-2918 re-pin is a clean, well-justified fix that preserves the original assertion's intent. The LOC breakdown is honest and reconciles against raw diff stats. No spec deviations found; the two items noted above are cosmetic/pre-existing and do not block approval.
